A.explanation: About $6.9\text{ m}$ is about half the required length and does not balance the $60\text{ N m}$ moment from the $6.0\text{ N}$ forces.

B.explanation: About $12\text{ m}$ is the value before dividing by $\sin 60^{\circ}$, so it omits the perpendicular component of the $5.0\text{ N}$ forces.

C.explanation: With $5 \times XY \times \sin 60^{\circ} = 60\text{ N m}$, $XY \approx 13.9\text{ m}$, which is $14\text{ m}$.

D.explanation: $24\text{ m}$ results from ignoring $\sin 60^{\circ}$ and doubling, giving twice the moment needed for zero resultant moment.

hints: Notice the two $6.0\text{ N}$ forces: one $7.0\text{ m}$ left of P acting up and one $3.0\text{ m}$ right of P acting down. Work out which way each turns about P.
The two $5.0\text{ N}$ horizontal forces at X and Y both turn the opposite way about P. Their combined moment depends on the total vertical separation of X and Y.
The rod XY makes $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, so the vertical separation is $XY \sin 60^{\circ}$. Set clockwise moments equal to anticlockwise moments for zero resultant moment.
walkthrough: Identify moments about P from the $6.0\text{ N}$ forces. Both produce a clockwise moment: left force gives $6.0 \times 7.0 = 42\text{ N m}$ and right force gives $6.0 \times 3.0 = 18\text{ N m}$.
Add them: total clockwise moment $= 42 + 18 = 60\text{ N m}$ about P.
State the balance rule: for no resultant moment, total anticlockwise moment must also be $60\text{ N m}$. This must come from the two $5.0\text{ N}$ forces at X and Y.

For a horizontal force, moment $=$ force $\times$ vertical distance from P. Let $PX = a$ and $PY = b$. Since XY is at $60^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, vertical distances are $a\sin 60^{\circ}$ and $b\sin 60^{\circ}$.
Set equal to $60\text{ N m}$: $5.0 \times XY \times \sin 60^{\circ} = 60$. So $XY = 12/\sin 60^{\circ} \approx 13.9\text{ m} \approx 14\text{ m}$. This is option C.
